paper.title: BanditSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via Bandit Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Speculative decoding hyperparameter selection, stochastic (stationary mean values)
unmapped: Rewards (accepted token counts) need not be independent: only the conditional mean given history and chosen arm is stationary (martingale structure)
Rewards take values in [1, L+1] where L is the maximum speculation length
Horizon is a random stopping time (rounds until EOS token generated); regret is the stopping-time regret E[ST(ALG)] - E[ST(ALG_{i*})]
settings.definition_quote: There exist $K$ values $\{\mu_i\}_{i\in[K]}\subset [1,L+1]$, such that conditioned on the history $\calH_{t-1}$ and the chosen arm $I_t$ at time $t$, the expected number of the accepted tokens $\bbE[Y_{I_t,t}\mid \calH_{t-1},I_t] = \mu_{I_t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Speculative decoding hyperparameter selection, stochastic, greedy decoding (lower bound)
unmapped: Conditional distribution of accepted length given history and arm i equals fixed P_{S_i} on {1,...,L+1} (Assumption D.2), with pairwise finite KL
Greedy decoding; asymptotics over a sequence of prompts whose generation length tends to infinity
Horizon is a random stopping time; stopping-time regret
settings.definition_quote: Given any bandit configuration ... conditional on the history $\calH_{t-1}$ and the selected arm $I_t$ at round $t$, the distribution of the length of the accepted tokens $\bbP(\;\cdot\mid \prompt,\calH_{t-1},I_t=i) = P_{S_i}(\,\cdot\,),\forall i\in[K]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Speculative decoding hyperparameter selection, oblivious adversarial (adversarial mean values, greedy decoding)
unmapped: Rewards are accepted token counts in [1, L+1] (rescaled bounded range)
Horizon is a random stopping time; regret E[ST(ALG)] - min_i ST(ALG_i) compares stopping times with different termination times
settings.definition_quote: Let the number of accepted tokens generated by hyperparameter $S_i$ at time step $t$ be $y_{i,t}=\len(X_{i,t})$. We assume $\{y_{i,t}\}_{i\in[K],t\in\bbN}$ is fixed by the environment before the algorithm starts.

symbols.L_spec: maximum speculation length L (rewards in [1, L+1])
symbols.E_len: expected length of the sequence generated by canonical decoding, E[len(pt_{tau_c})]

source.label: thm:stoc_up
source.quote:
Under Assumptions~ef{ass:mean} and~ef{ass:finiteLen}, given any prompt $\prompt\in\calX^*$ and bandit configuration $
u$, the expected stopping time regret of Algorithm~ef{algo:SDbandit} with $\alg=\,$Algorithm~ef{alg:SpecDecUCB} ($\specucb$) is upper bounded as $\Reg(\alg,\prompt,
u) = O(mH(\prompt,
u)\cdot L^2 \log bE[\len(\prompt_{	au_{mc}})])$.

results.notes: Quantity is the stopping-time regret (expected number of speculative decoding rounds vs best fixed hyperparameter), mapped to 'other'. H = sum_{i != i*} 1/(mu_{i*} Delta_i). The log of expected length plays the role of log T.

symbols.len_m: length of the sequence generated by canonical decoding from prompt pt^m

conditions: non-anticipatory and consistent arm selection algorithm
Kinf_i here is kl_i := inf_{S in calS} {KL(P_{S_i}, P_S): E_{P_S}[X] > mu_{i*}}

source.label: thm:stocLwBd
source.quote:
Given any sequence of initial prompts $(\prompt^m)_{m=1}^\infty$ with $\len(\prompt^m_{	au_{mc}})	o \infty$ and a bandit configuration $
u$, under Assumption~ef{ass:meanAugmented}, the greedy decoding strategy and the dynamics represented in Algorithm~ef{algo:SDbandit}, for any non-anticipatory and consistent arm selection algorithm $\alg$, the expected regret satisfies $\liminf_{m	o\infty}  rac{\Reg(\alg,\prompt,
u)}{\log(\len(\prompt_{	au_{mc}}^m))} \geq \sum_{i
eq i^*}  rac{\Delta_i}{\mu_{i^*}}\cdot  rac{1}{\mathrm{kl}_i}$

results.notes: Paper's kl_i is a K_inf-type quantity over the hyperparameter set, mapped to Kinf_i.

symbols.p_geo: truncated-geometric parameter p_{i*} of the optimal hyperparameter
symbols.len_m: length of the sequence generated by canonical decoding from prompt pt^m

conditions: all hyperparameters have truncated geometric accepted-length distributions on [1, L+1]

source.label: prop:stoc_tightness
source.quote: Let $\calS_{\mathrm{TGD}}=\{S:P_S \mbox{ satisfies \eqref{equ:truncatedGeo}}\}$. Let $\{S_i\}_{i=1}^K\subset \calS_{\mathrm{TGD}}$ ... then $\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac{\Reg(\alg,\prompt^m,\nu)}{\log(\len(\prompt_{\tau_{\rmc}}^m))}\geq \rmH(\prompt,\nu) \cdot \frac{p_{i^*}(1-p_{i^*}^L)}{(1-p_{i^*})}$. Therefore, the upper and lower bound match up absolute constants and a $\frac{L^2(1-p_{i^*})}{p_{i^*}(1-p_{i^*}^L)}$ factor.

results.notes: If p_{i*} in (2^{-1/L},1), bound becomes sum 1/(mu* Delta_i) * L/2 (stated in proof).

bound.expression_latex: 2L\cdot \min\bigg\{\sqrt{\len(\prompt_{\tau_\rmc}) K\log K}, 2L K\log K + \sqrt{\min_{i\in[K]}\ST(\alg_i)  K\log K} \bigg\}

symbols.len_c: length of the sequence generated by canonical (greedy) decoding
symbols.ST_min: stopping time of the best fixed hyperparameter, min_i ST(ALG_i)

source.label: thm:adv_UpBd
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:finiteLen}, ~\ref{ass:adv_mean} and~\ref{ass:stop}, given any prompt $\prompt\in\calX^*$ and bandit configuration $\nu$, the expected stopping time regret of Algorithm~\ref{algo:SDbandit} with $\alg=\,$Algorithm~\ref{alg:SpecDecEXP3} (\specexp{}), $\Reg(\alg,\prompt,\nu) \le 2L\cdot \min\{\sqrt{\len(\prompt_{\tau_\rmc}) K\log K}, 2L K\log K + \sqrt{\min_{i\in[K]}\ST(\alg_i)  K\log K} \}$.

results.notes: Stopping-time regret (mapped to 'other'). Remark D.1 gives a similar bound with expectations under sampling decoding (not recorded separately). Combines a worst-case-like and instance-dependent term; dependence labelled instance_dependent.
